status.en: 12 armed incidents reported in the past seven days, most of them in Rumbek, Nyang and Juba.
status.nb: 12 væpnede hendelser meldt de siste sju dagene, flest i Rumbek, Nyang og Juba.

summary.en: Communal clashes have intensified in Lakes state, prompting a curfew and a visit by caretaker governor Rin Tueny, while UNMISS has increased civilian protection after deadly attacks in Rumbek. SSPDF soldiers were wounded in an assault on a Mundri West military outpost and the U.S. Embassy condemned an assault on WFP workers in Jonglei that involved looting of aid. An AIC cleric was shot dead in Juba and a Juba High Court sentenced five officers to 24 years for raiding a general's home. SPLA-IO forces retook Akobo after a deadly dawn clash. The lethal communal violence now far exceeds the two battle-related deaths in 2024, according to UCDP.
summary.nb: Kommunale sammenstøt har økt i Lakes-delstaten, noe som har ført til portforbud og et besøk av vikar-gouverneur Rin Tueny, mens UNMISS har styrket sivile beskyttelsestiltak etter dødelige angrep i Rumbek. SSPDF-soldater ble såret i et angrep på en militærpost i Mundri West, og den amerikanske ambassaden fordømte et angrep på WFP-arbeidere i Jonglei som innebar plyndring av hjelp. En AIC-prest ble skutt og drept i Juba, og Juba høyesterett dømte fem offiserer til 24 år for å ha ransaket en generals bolig. SPLA-IO-styrker tok Akobo tilbake etter et dødelig sammenstøt ved daggry. Den dødelige kommunale volden overstiger nå langt de to kamprelaterte dødsfallene i 2024, ifølge UCDP.

background.title: South Sudanese Civil War
background.extract: The South Sudanese Civil War was a multi-sided civil war in South Sudan fought from 2013 to 2018 between government and opposition forces. The civil war caused rampant human rights abuses, including forced displacement, ethnic massacres, and killings of journalists by various parties. Since the war's end, South Sudan has been governed by a coalition formed by leaders of the former warring factions, Salva Kiir Mayardit and Riek Machar. The country continues to recover from the war while experiencing ongoing and systemic ethnic violence.
